messages:
ravi: FYI we just got a DSAR from an EU subject requesting erasure for acct: EU-77b2. Legal looped in. Asking for full wipe across vectors, backups, and any analytical snapshots.

tess: Can someone map where embeddings and derivative artifacts live? We have faiss-index shards in prod, nightly s3 snapshots, and cold archives in Glacier Deep Archive (eu-west-1). There may also be analytics exports in redwood-analytics bucket.

jamie-backup: Confirmed: faiss shards live on fs-vec nodes (eu cluster), nightly dump to s3://redwood-backups/eu-shards/, cross-region replication to s3://redwood-backups-eu-west/. Glacier vault eu-west-1 contains monthly archives for 2 years. EBS snapshots for ml-cluster-12 include incremental chain.

andrew-legal: We verified identity (gov ID) and requester control. No active preservation order. GDPR timeline: reasonable timeframe; we should aim for completion and evidence within 30 days, but operational SLA we try for 72 hours for live stores. Legal: will accept deletion_proof bundle with signed audit log and manifest.

ravi: KMS: backups encrypted with CMK arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111122223333:key/abcd-1234. Question: do we disable key or rotate? Thoughts?

sec-bot: Automated checklist: do NOT disable or schedule key deletion. Recommended flow: (1) delete blobs/objects and mark records deleted in DB, (2) emit signed deletion manifest referencing kms_key_id, (3) retain key for audit and possible forensics. See: https://redwood.internal/sec/dsar-guidelines

ops-runbook: For cold archives (Glacier), deletion may require vault inventory and job submissions. Glacier Deep Archive has retrieval delays (~12h+) and delete-once-retrieved semantics. Could incur costs. We need to check retention policies and any Object Lock/legal holds on the bucket.

tess: Edge case: analytics exports contain derived tokens with hashed subject_id. Those may be brittle to find. Querying analytics may require cross-team ticket.

jamie-backup: Technical constraints: EBS snapshot chains are shared dedup chains. Removing a snapshot can be done but must preserve chain integrity for unrelated volumes. Backup-controller supports tombstone tagging (tag:erased=true) and background chain-sweep to remove orphaned deltas after verification. That sweep window defaults to 7 days.

ravi: Operational proposal: create ephemeral IAM role erase-role:sts that allows s3:DeleteObject/PutObjectTagging on specific prefixes + ec2:DeleteSnapshot and lambda:InvokeFunction for tidy operations. Role must be assumable only by the dsar-cleaner service and require MFA or signed DSAR request id in session tag.

sec-bot: Policy caveat: avoid wildcard deletion and require Resource ARNs with account prefix and subject tag condition. Example condition: "StringEquals": {"aws:RequestTag/subject_id":"EU-77b2"}. Keep least privilege and short TTL for role creds.

andrew-legal: If we cannot fully remove archived copies within legal timeframe, file a retention-exception request with justification and timeline. Legal needs the exception text and expected completion date. Exception will be a documented temporary hold in the governance tracker.

tess: For faiss indexes we also need to reindex the shard to remove vectors. Options: (A) in-place vector deletion + compact, (B) rebuild index without subject vectors. In-place deletes are supported but may leave tombstones until compaction. Rebuild is safer for correctness but heavier.

ravi: Recommended path: live stores (faiss, DB) first — delete vectors and mark record deleted; emit audit log immediately. Then schedule cross-region S3 object deletions and Glacier jobs. EBS snapshot chain: tag snapshots owner=dsar-subject-EU-77b2, run backup-controller chain-sweep with careful validation.

ops-runbook: I can draft a runbook. Steps: 1) Verify identity & create DSAR ticket 2) Create short-lived erase-role session using DSAR request tag 3) Run vector delete job on eu cluster 4) Run s3 deletes for prefixes and replication targets 5) Submit Glacier archive ID delete job and wait for completion 6) Tag EBS snapshots and run chain-sweep 7) Produce signed manifest + upload to s3://redwood-audit/dsar/2025/ 8) Notify legal and requester.

jamie-backup: Note: if object-lock retention or bucket-level holds exist we need to escalate to storage-team; that can block deletion and triggers retention exception flow.

andrew-legal: If storage-team finds retention holds for regulatory reasons, legal will require the hold reason and end-date; otherwise we approve exception for mechanical delay if documented.

ravi: Quick sample IAM snippet (outline):
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["s3:DeleteObject","s3:PutObjectTagging"],"Resource":["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-backups/eu-shards/EU-77b2/*"],"Condition":{"StringEquals":{"aws:RequestTag/subject_id":"EU-77b2"}}},
    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["ec2:DeleteSnapshot"],"Resource":["*"] ,"Condition":{"StringEquals":{"ec2:ResourceTag/subject_id":"EU-77b2"}}}
  ]
}
```

sec-bot: Remember to include an auditable signed statement for every deletion operation containing: actor_principal, assumed_role_arn, request_id, resources, pre_delete_digest, post_delete_digest, kms_key_id, timestamp, signature. Store under locked audit bucket with MFA-delete disabled only for governance admins.

tess: Action items: - jamie to enumerate archives + provide archive IDs and estimated deletion times - ops to draft ephemeral erase-role + policy PR - infra-bot to open INFRA ticket for TTL creds and tagging requirement - security to finalize manifest schema - legal to prepare statement template for deletion_proof.

infra-bot: Created ticket INFRA-8790 for ephemeral-role + tagging enforcement. Created ticket BACKUP-4437 for archive enumeration.

andrew-legal: Once manifest is uploaded, legal will verify and sign the deletion certificate. Please include hashes for deleted blobs where possible.

ravi: Thanks everyone. I'll queue DSAR-EU-77b2 in the dsar-cleaner runbook and coordinate the first pass for live stores today. Will update timeline in the ticket.
